warning: Vaccine rules changed in 2025-2026. Re-check official sources before relying on this.

general_sources.says: Private plans must cover certain vaccines with no copay in-network; Part B covers COVID-19, flu, pneumococcal, hepatitis B for people at increased risk; Part D makes all other CDC-recommended adult vaccines available at no cost; most adults with Medicaid get all CDC-recommended vaccines at no cost. (Updated Sept 2, 2026)
Part D covers all commercially available vaccines not covered by Part B; $0 for ACIP-recommended adult vaccines; non-ACIP-recommended vaccines may have cost sharing.
Adult immunizations plans must cover: chickenpox, diphtheria, flu, hepatitis A, hepatitis B, HPV, measles, meningococcal, mumps, whooping cough, pneumococcal, rubella, shingles, tetanus.
Adult schedule page still shows the 2025 schedule (addendum July 2, 2025); no 2026 adult schedule found.

massachusetts_rule.rule: Massachusetts Bulletin 2025-03 (Division of Insurance and Department of Public Health, issued September 3, 2025)
massachusetts_rule.coverage: Insurers must cover vaccines recommended by the Massachusetts Department of Public Health (DPH), not only CDC recommendations.
massachusetts_rule.cost: No cost-sharing and no utilization management (no prior authorization delays) for covered routine vaccines.
massachusetts_rule.applies_to: Fully insured health plans issued under Massachusetts law (for example Blue Cross Blue Shield of Massachusetts and HMOs). Group Insurance Commission (GIC) plans and MassHealth also cover vaccines according to DPH guidelines.
massachusetts_rule.does_not_apply_to: Self-insured employer plans are not required to follow the bulletin.
massachusetts_rule.patient_message: If your plan is through a large employer, check with your plan, because it may not have to follow the Massachusetts rule.
massachusetts_rule.brands: Insurers may cover only certain brands, as long as at least one product covers each DPH-recommended vaccine.
massachusetts_rule.verification: verified via web search, 2026-10-23 (mass.gov could not be opened directly)

medicare.coverage: Part D covers commercially available vaccines needed to prevent illness. Part B covers it only to treat an exposure.
medicare.cost: $0 under Part D if ACIP recommends it for you; otherwise the plan may charge a copay (CMS)

commercial.coverage: Hepatitis A is on HealthCare.gov's adult preventive list ('recommended populations vary'). Coverage for travel only: not found.
commercial.cost: No copay or coinsurance in-network for covered preventive services; '$0 cost isn't guaranteed in all cases.'

massachusetts.coverage: The bulletin covers routine vaccines only. Travel vaccines (hepatitis A for travel, typhoid, yellow fever) are not part of it. Check with your plan.
massachusetts.verification: verified via web search, 2026-10-23 (mass.gov could not be opened directly)

notes: CDC: travelers to countries where hepatitis A is common should get vaccinated.
Travel vaccines are often not covered by insurance. CDC: 'many health insurance plans provide no or limited coverage for travel immunizations.' Call your plan first.
